title: &self vs self
prompt: In an `impl` block, what is the difference between a method taking `&self` and one taking `self`?
answer: `&self` borrows: the caller keeps the value and can call the method again. `self` consumes: the value moves into the method, so a second call on the same value is E0382, use of moved value.

example.code:
fn cost(&self) -> u32 { .. }
fn into_label(self) -> String { .. }
example.caption: &self is callable twice; self consumes the value.
